subjects.name: P2 · Unit 6 – System Software & Operating Systems

sets.name: 1 · Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers

questions.question: The role of a compiler in software development is

options.B: To convert high level code to machine code
options.C: To debug errors in the code

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into machine (object) code. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q78

questions.question: A compiler is used for

options.A: Converting machine language to high level programming language
options.B: Converting high level programming language to machine language

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Translation goes from the high-level source to machine language. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q67

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the example/examples of low-level programming language?
(a) Python
(b) Java
(c) C
(d) Machine language
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Machine (and assembly) language are low-level; KEA's key treats C as a high-level language. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q73

questions.question:
Match the following:
Generation of Languages: a) Second generation language  b) Third generation language  c) Fourth generation language  d) Fifth generation language
Example: i. Prolog  ii. FoxPro  iii. Assembler  iv. Pascal

options.A: a – iii, b – iv, c – ii, d – i
options.B: a – ii, b – iii, c – iv, d – i
options.C: a – iv, b – iii, c – ii, d – i
options.D: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: 2GL assembly, 3GL procedural languages such as Pascal, 4GL database/query tools such as FoxPro, 5GL logic languages such as Prolog. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Technician Gr-III CS (C1) · Q85

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered as an essential part of a computer system's hardware?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A compiler is system software, not hardware. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q68

questions.question: Which of the following helps Assembler to deal with branching code?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: The first pass builds the symbol table, so forward branch targets are known in the second pass. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
questions.source: KSET 2023 CS&A · Q59

questions.question: A symbol table in assembler contains

options.A: Mapping of variables and their memory addresses

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: The symbol table maps labels and symbols to addresses; opcodes are in the machine-opcode table. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
questions.source: KSET 2025 CS&A · Q79

questions.question: Machine language is:

options.C: Binary instructions that the CPU executes directly; it is machine-dependent
options.D: A language that needs a compiler

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It needs no translation, but is very hard to write.

questions.question: Assembly language uses ____ and is translated into machine code by a(n) ____.

options.C: Mnemonics such as MOV and ADD; assembler

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each assembly statement usually maps to one machine instruction.

questions.question: A key difference between a compiler and an interpreter is that:

options.B: An interpreter produces an object file
options.C: A compiler executes line by line
options.D: A compiler translates the whole program before execution; an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Compiled programs usually run faster; interpreters make debugging easier.

questions.question: An interpreter, on meeting an error in line 20 of a program:

options.C: Reports all errors before running anything

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A compiler reports errors for the whole program before any of it runs.

questions.question: The usual order of the phases of a compiler is:

options.A: Syntax analysis → lexical analysis → code generation → optimization
options.B: Semantic analysis → lexical analysis → parsing → code generation
options.C: Code generation → lexical analysis → parsing → optimization
options.D: Lexical analysis → syntax analysis → semantic analysis → intermediate code → code optimization → code generation

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The symbol table and error handler are used by all phases.

questions.question: The lexical analyzer (scanner) of a compiler produces:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: The parser (syntax analyzer) then builds a parse tree from the tokens.

questions.question: A cross-compiler is a compiler that:

options.A: Translates between two high-level languages only
options.B: Runs only on the target machine
options.D: Runs on one machine but produces code for a different machine

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Used to build software for embedded systems.

questions.question: In a two-pass assembler, the main task of pass 1 is to:

options.A: Assign addresses to all statements using the location counter and build the symbol table

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Pass 2 uses the symbol table to generate the object code.

questions.question: Using a label in an instruction before the label is defined is called a:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: One-pass assemblers handle it with back-patching.

questions.question: Assembler directives (pseudo-ops) such as START, END and EQU:

options.B: Give instructions to the assembler and do not themselves become machine instructions

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). DC/DS (or DB/DW) reserve or define storage.

questions.question: The table that holds the mnemonic opcodes and their machine codes in an assembler is the:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Labels and their addresses are in the symbol table.

questions.question: In an assembler, the location counter is used to:

options.D: Keep track of the address of the next instruction or data item

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: It is advanced by the length of each instruction.

questions.question: In Java, the compiler javac translates source code into:

options.A: Bytecode, which the Java Virtual Machine interprets or compiles just-in-time
options.D: Native machine code for one CPU only

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: This gives 'write once, run anywhere' portability.

questions.question: A program that converts machine code back into assembly language is a:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A decompiler tries to recover high-level source.

questions.question:
Match the translator with its job:
a. Assembler
b. Compiler
c. Interpreter
d. Cross-compiler

1. Translates a whole high-level program into object code
2. Translates assembly language into machine code
3. Produces code for a different machine
4. Translates and runs statement by statement
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Translator matching is common in KEA papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Machine language is machine-dependent.
II. Assembly language programs run unchanged on every type of processor.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Assembly language is specific to a processor family.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A two-pass assembler handles forward references easily.
Reason (R): Pass 1 records the addresses of all labels in the symbol table.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Pass 2 can then fill in every address.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): An interpreter produces a separate object file that can be run later without the interpreter.
Reason (R): An interpreter translates and executes a program statement by statement.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: No object file is produced, so A is false.

questions.question: Which of these is a high-level language?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: High-level languages are close to human language and machine-independent.

questions.question: Code optimization in a compiler aims to:

options.D: Make the target code faster or smaller without changing what the program does

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: It works on intermediate code and/or target code.

questions.question: A missing semicolon in a C statement is detected during:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Type mismatches and undeclared variables are found in semantic analysis.

questions.question: Literals such as =F'5' in an assembly program are collected by the assembler in the:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: They are placed in a literal pool, e.g. at an LTORG statement.

questions.question: Writing a compiler for a language in that same language, and using a simpler version to compile it, is called:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Most C compilers are themselves written in C.

sets.name: 2 · Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software

questions.question: What is the role of linker in compilation?

options.A: Translates source code to object code

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The linker combines object modules and libraries into one executable, resolving external references. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
questions.source: KSET 2025 CS&A · Q23

questions.question:
In the process of macro expansion given:
S₁: lexical substitution implies replacement of a character string by another string during program generation
S₂: lexical substitution is employed to replace occurrences of formal parameters by some random values
Which of the following holds good?

options.A: Both S₁ and S₂ are true
options.B: Both S₁ and S₂ are false
options.C: S₁ is false and S₂ is true
options.D: S₁ is true and S₂ is false

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Formal parameters are replaced by the actual parameters of the call, not by random values (Dhamdhere). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
questions.source: KSET 2025 CS&A · Q41

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/statements about software is/are correct?
(a) Software can be categorized into system software and application software
(b) System software includes operating system and device drives
(c) Application software includes software for tasks like word processing
(d) All system and application softwares are open-sources
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Much software is proprietary, so (d) is false. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q77

questions.question:
Match the following software with their respective categories
Software: (a) Microsoft Word  (b) Ubuntu Linux  (c) Eclipse IDE  (d) Norton Antivirus
Category: i) Application software  ii) Development software  iii) Utility software  iv) System software

options.A: a – iv, b – ii, c – iii, d – i
options.B: a – ii, b – i, c – iii, d – iv
options.C: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv
options.D: a – i, b – iv, c – ii, d – iii

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Word – application; Ubuntu – system (OS); Eclipse – development; Norton – utility. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q80

questions.question: Which of the following softwares is considered as application software?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Operating systems and firmware are system software. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of system software?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: An operating system is system software. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q75

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of application software?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: A web browser is an application program. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q82

questions.question: Static linking differs from dynamic linking because in static linking:

options.B: Library code is copied into the executable at link time; in dynamic linking shared libraries (.dll, .so) are linked at load or run time
options.D: Linking happens while the program is running

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Dynamic linking saves memory and lets libraries be updated without relinking.

questions.question: A loader is the system program that:

options.D: Places an executable program into main memory and prepares it for execution

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Loading is the last step before execution.

questions.question: The four functions of a loader are:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Classic textbook list (Donovan).

questions.question: Relocation means:

options.A: Copying a program to another computer
options.C: Adjusting the address-dependent parts of a program so it can run from a memory area other than the one assumed when it was translated

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Relocation bits or modification records tell the loader which words to adjust.

questions.question: An absolute loader:

options.B: Loads the program at the address fixed by the assembler, with no relocation

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Simple, but the programmer must know where the program will be loaded.

questions.question: The small program, stored in ROM/firmware, that starts loading the operating system when a computer is switched on is the:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It loads the boot loader or kernel from disk.

questions.question: A 'compile-and-go' (assemble-and-go) loader:

options.A: Places the translated code directly in memory and starts execution, without producing an object file

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Fast, but the program must be translated again every time it is run.

questions.question: Dynamic loading means that:

options.A: Loading is done by the compiler
options.B: All routines are loaded at start
options.D: A routine is loaded into memory only when it is first called

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Unused routines (e.g. error handlers) are never loaded.

questions.question: A macro is:

options.A: A subroutine called at run time with a return address
options.B: A named group of statements that is substituted (expanded) wherever its name is used

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Macro expansion is done by a macro processor (pre-processor) before translation.

questions.question: Compared with a subroutine call, a macro call:

options.C: Is expanded in-line at every use, making the program larger but avoiding call/return overhead
options.D: Keeps a single copy of the code

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Subroutines keep one copy and use CALL/RETURN.

questions.question: In assembler macro definitions, the body of the macro lies between the pseudo-ops:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The macro name and its formal parameters follow MACRO.

questions.question: The tables maintained by a two-pass macro processor include:

options.C: Macro Name Table (MNT), Macro Definition Table (MDT) and Argument List Array (ALA)

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: MNT points into the MDT for each macro.

questions.question: A debugger is a tool that helps a programmer to:

options.B: Find and fix errors using breakpoints, single-stepping and inspection of variables

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). e.g. gdb, or the debugger built into an IDE.

questions.question: A breakpoint in debugging is:

options.A: A marked point where program execution pauses so the programmer can examine its state
options.C: The last line of the program

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Execution can then be continued or stepped.

questions.question:
Match the system program with its role:
a. Loader
b. Linker
c. Macro processor
d. Debugger

1. Places the program in memory for execution
2. Combines object modules and resolves external references
3. Expands macro calls
4. Helps locate errors with breakpoints
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). System-program matching appears in KSET papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A macro call is replaced by the macro body during expansion.
II. A subroutine's body is copied into the program at every call.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: A subroutine has a single copy reached by CALL.

questions.question: An external reference in an object module is:

options.A: A use of a symbol defined in another module, which the linker resolves

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: EXTRN / ENTRY (or extern / global) declarations mark such symbols.

questions.question: The output of a linker is typically a(n):
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The loader then brings the executable into memory.

questions.question: Utility software includes programs such as:

options.C: Antivirus, disk defragmenter, backup and file-compression tools

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Utilities help maintain and optimise the computer.

questions.question: A device driver is classified as:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: It lets the OS control a particular device.

questions.question: Conditional macro expansion (e.g. AIF and AGO in IBM assembler) allows:

options.A: Macros to be called at run time
options.D: Different statements to be generated depending on the macro's arguments

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The expansion-time variables and labels are processed by the macro processor.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Relocation is needed when a program is loaded at an address different from the one assumed during translation.
Reason (R): Address-sensitive instructions contain addresses computed from the assumed origin.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The loader adds the difference to each such address.

questions.question: In system programming, a text editor is used to:

options.A: Create and modify source programs and other text files

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: e.g. vi, nano, Notepad.

sets.name: 1 · Operating System Functions, Types and Structure

questions.question: A set of programs that controls the resources of a system and provides it to the users with an interface that is easier to use is called
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: The OS manages resources and offers a convenient interface. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q89

questions.question: Which one among the following is not a basic function of operating system?
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Virus protection is done by separate utility (antivirus) software. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary goal of an operating system?

options.A: To provide a platform for running applications

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: KEA's key: the OS is above all a resource manager. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q48

questions.question: Which one of the following is not true?

options.A: Kernel remains in the memory during the entire computer session.
options.B: Kernel is made of various modules which cannot be loaded in running operating system.
options.C: Kernel is the first part of the operating system to load into the memory during booting.
options.D: Kernel is the program that constitutes the central core of the operating system.

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Modern kernels such as Linux support loadable modules that can be added while the system runs. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q4

questions.question:
Match the following:
Operating System: a) Android  b) Windows Operating System  c) Linux  d) OS-X
Companies: i. Microsoft  ii. Google  iii. Apple  iv. Open source

options.A: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
options.B: a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
options.C: a - iii, b - i, c - ii, d - iv
options.D: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Android – Google; Windows – Microsoft; Linux – open source; OS X (macOS) – Apple. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q9

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are open source operating system?
(a) Linux  (b) Opensolaris
(c) BSD  (d) Android
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: All four are open source (Android's core is the Android Open Source Project). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q79

questions.question: An example of non-real-time systems is
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: E-mail has no strict deadlines; the others need guaranteed response times. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which one of the following errors will be handled by the operating system?

options.D: Failure of power, connection and Lack of paper

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Error detection is an OS service covering hardware, I/O devices and the network. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Lecturer CS · Q49

questions.question: An operating system acts as:

options.A: An intermediary between the user and the computer hardware, and a manager of its resources

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Silberschatz: the OS is a resource allocator and a control program.

questions.question: In a batch operating system:

options.A: Strict deadlines must always be met
options.B: Similar jobs are grouped and run one after another without user interaction
options.D: Users interact with programs while they run

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Early mainframes used batch processing with punched cards.

questions.question: Multiprogramming means:

options.A: Running one program at a time
options.C: Keeping several jobs in memory so the CPU can switch to another job when one waits for I/O
options.D: Using many CPUs for one job

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Its aim is to increase CPU utilisation.

questions.question: A time-sharing (multitasking) system:

options.D: Switches the CPU among users' programs so quickly that each user gets fast interactive response

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each process receives a short time slice (quantum).

questions.question: A hard real-time system is one in which:

options.A: Missing a deadline is a system failure, e.g. an airbag controller or a pacemaker

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). In soft real-time systems, such as video streaming, an occasional missed deadline is tolerable.

questions.question: Privileged instructions, such as I/O and timer management, can be executed only in:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A mode bit in hardware tells which mode the CPU is in.

questions.question: In a monolithic kernel:

options.A: Most OS services run together in a single address space in kernel mode
options.B: Only message passing is in the kernel
options.D: Every service is a user program

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Traditional UNIX and Linux are monolithic (Linux with loadable modules).

questions.question: A microkernel design:

options.A: Puts all drivers in the kernel
options.C: Keeps only essential functions (IPC, basic scheduling, memory) in the kernel and runs other services in user space

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Examples: Mach, QNX, MINIX 3. It is more reliable but message passing adds overhead.

questions.question: In the layered approach to OS design:

options.A: All layers can call each other freely
options.B: Each layer uses only the services of the layers below it; layer 0 is the hardware

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's THE system used this structure.

questions.question: Windows NT-based systems and macOS are usually described as having a:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: They combine features of monolithic and microkernel designs.

questions.question: SPOOLING stands for:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Print jobs are spooled to disk and printed one by one.

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Both are standard facts.

questions.question:

options.C: A is true, but R is false

questions.question: Symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) means:

options.A: Every processor runs the OS and all processors are peers

questions.question: A distributed operating system:

options.B: Manages networked computers so that they appear to users as one system
options.C: Runs on a single CPU only

questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It shares resources and computation across machines.

questions.question: The program that reads and carries out typed user commands, such as bash in Linux, is the:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Windows has cmd.exe and PowerShell.

questions.question: Loadable kernel modules in Linux allow:

options.C: Drivers and file systems to be added to or removed from the running kernel
options.D: User programs to run in kernel mode

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: This gives a monolithic kernel some of a microkernel's flexibility.

questions.question: Which of these is an embedded / real-time operating system?
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: FreeRTOS and QNX are other examples.

questions.question: The main disadvantage of a microkernel compared with a monolithic kernel is:

options.C: Extra overhead from message passing between user-space services

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Each service request may need several context switches.

sets.name: 2 · OS Services, System Calls and Booting

questions.question: To access the services of the operating system, the interface is provided by
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: System calls are the interface between a running program and the OS kernel. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q3

questions.question:
Match the following types of system calls with their description
System calls: a. Process control  b. File management  c. Device management  d. Information maintenance
Description: i. Creates and deletes files  ii. Schedules and terminates processes  iii. Performs input and output operations.  iv. Retrieves system status information

options.A: a – ii, b – i, c – iii, d – iv
options.B: a – iii, b – i, c – ii, d – iv
options.C: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Process control – create/terminate processes; file management – create/delete files; device management – I/O; information maintenance – time, date, system data. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q42

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of system call?
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting

questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q49

questions.question:
Considering the following statements, choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Software drivers enable the operating system to communicate with hardware system.
Reason (R): Without the appropriate drivers, an operating system cannot operate hardware devices.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Drivers translate the OS's generic requests into device-specific commands. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q72

questions.question: The ____ presents a uniform device access interface to the IO subsystem, much as system calls provide a standard interface between the application and the operating system
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Silberschatz: device drivers hide device differences from the I/O subsystem. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Lecturer CS · Q46

questions.question: Where is BIOS usually stored?

options.A: Flash memory on the mother board

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: BIOS/UEFI firmware lives in flash ROM on the motherboard. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q69

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of system booting?

options.A: POST → BOOT DEVICE SELECTION → LOADING OS → BIOS
options.B: POST → BIOS → BOOT DEVICE SELECTION → LOADING OS
options.C: BOOT DEVICE SELECTION → BIOS → POST → LOADING OS
options.D: BOOT DEVICE SELECTION → POST → BIOS → LOADING OS

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: KEA's key: POST, then the BIOS hands over to the boot device, which loads the OS. (Strictly, POST is itself run by the BIOS.) (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q75

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of BIOS used in modern systems?
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: UEFI has replaced the legacy BIOS on modern PCs. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q76

questions.question: Which of these is a service provided by an operating system?

options.D: Program execution, I/O operations, file-system manipulation, communication and error detection

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Also resource allocation, accounting, and protection and security.

questions.question: A system call:

options.B: Is a phone call to the system administrator
options.C: Is the way a program requests a service from the OS kernel; it switches the CPU from user mode to kernel mode

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is implemented with a trap (software interrupt).

questions.question: fork(), exec(), wait() and exit() in UNIX are examples of ____ system calls.
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). fork() creates a child process; exec() loads a new program into it.

questions.question: open(), read(), write() and close() are examples of ____ system calls.
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: The same calls are used for many devices in UNIX.

questions.question: getpid(), alarm() and sleep() in UNIX belong to the ____ category of system calls.
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Windows equivalents include GetCurrentProcessID() and SetTimer().

questions.question: The Windows system call that corresponds to UNIX fork() for creating a process is:
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Silberschatz lists Windows and UNIX equivalents side by side.

questions.question: Application programmers usually call system services through an API such as POSIX or the Windows API because:

options.B: APIs run faster than the hardware
options.C: APIs are portable and hide the details of the actual system calls

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The run-time library turns API functions into system calls.

questions.question: Parameters can be passed to the OS in a system call:

options.A: In registers, in a block or table in memory whose address is in a register, or on the stack

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Linux and Solaris combine registers and memory blocks.

questions.question: On most PCs, the first sector of a boot disk (512 bytes) that holds the boot loader and partition table in the legacy scheme is the:
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: UEFI systems use the GUID Partition Table (GPT) instead.

questions.question: GRUB is:

options.D: A boot loader commonly used to start Linux

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It can offer a menu to choose between several operating systems.

questions.question: After the Linux kernel is loaded and initialised, the first user-space process it starts (PID 1) is:
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: It starts all other services.

questions.question: Restarting a computer that is already on, without switching off the power, is called a:
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A cold boot starts from power off.

questions.question: Separating policy from mechanism in OS design means:

options.A: The mechanism decides how something is done; the policy decides what is done, so policies can change without changing mechanisms
options.B: Policies are written in assembly only

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: e.g. a timer is a mechanism; how long a time slice should be is a policy.

questions.question:
Match the UNIX system call with its category:
a. fork()
b. open()
c. ioctl()
d. getpid()

1. Information maintenance
2. File management
3. Process control
4. Device management
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A frequent matching question.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A system call switches the CPU from user mode to kernel mode.
II. The bootstrap program is stored in RAM before the computer is switched on.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: RAM is empty at power-on; the bootstrap is in ROM/flash firmware.

questions.question: pipe(), shmget() and send()/recv() are examples of ____ system calls.
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Message passing and shared memory are the two communication models.

questions.question: chmod() and umask() in UNIX are examples of ____ system calls.
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: They control access permissions on files.

questions.question: POST (Power-On Self-Test) is performed to:

options.B: Check that essential hardware such as memory, keyboard and video works before the OS is loaded

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Beep codes report failures.

questions.question: CMOS memory on the motherboard stores:

options.D: BIOS settings such as date, time and boot order, kept alive by a small battery

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Removing the battery resets these settings.

questions.question: An operating system's user interface can be:
questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: Many systems offer more than one.

questions.question: Most modern operating systems are written mainly in:

options.A: C and C++, with small parts in assembly language

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: High-level languages make the OS easier to port and maintain.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Application programs normally reach the kernel only through system calls.
Reason (R): User-mode programs cannot execute privileged instructions directly.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: OS Services, System Calls and Booting
questions.explanation: The trap into kernel mode is controlled by the OS.

sets.name: 1 · Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of different states of process in operating system.
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: A process is admitted to ready, dispatched to running, may wait for I/O, and finally terminates. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q14

questions.question: In a time share operating system, when the time slot assigned to a process is completed, the process switches from current state to ____.
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: A timer interrupt preempts the running process and puts it back in the ready queue. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q5

questions.question: What is the ready state of a process?

options.C: Process is waiting to be assigned to a CPU
options.D: The process is waiting for some event to occur

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: New = being created; running = executing; waiting = waiting for an event; ready = waiting for the CPU. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Technician Gr-III CS (C1) · Q26

questions.question:
When a program is loaded into the memory and it becomes a process, it can be divided into which of the section?
i. Stack  ii. Heap  iii. Text  iv. Data
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: A process in memory has text (code), data, heap and stack sections. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Lecturer CS · Q50

questions.question:
A process current activity is represented by
i. Program counter
ii. Contents of process register
iii. Stack
iv. Data section
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Silberschatz: the current activity is represented by the value of the program counter and the contents of the processor's registers. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Lecturer CS · Q51

questions.question:
Order the following steps of process creation in an operating system.
a. Assigning a Process Control Block (PCB) to the process
b. Loading the process in memory
c. Assigning the process ID
d. Creating a new entry in process table
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: KEA's key: give the process an ID, make its process-table entry, set up its PCB, then load it into memory. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q40

questions.question: In a computer system that consists of n number of CPUs, the maximum processes that can exist in the ready state would be
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: At most n processes can be running, but any number may wait in the ready queue. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q7

questions.question: Which of the following does not interrupt a running process?
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: The scheduler runs only after an interrupt or system call gives control to the OS; it does not itself interrupt a process. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q95

questions.question: The total time taken for switching between the user & the Kernel modes of execution is t₁, while the total time taken for switching between two processes is t₂. Out of the following, which one is true?

options.D: we cannot say anything about the relation between t₂ & t₁

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: A process switch includes a mode switch plus saving and restoring the whole context, so it takes longer. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q17

questions.question: A process is best defined as:

options.A: A set of instructions on paper

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A program is a passive entity; a process is active, with a program counter and resources.

questions.question: A running process moves to the waiting (blocked) state when it:

options.C: Is admitted by the long-term scheduler
options.D: Requests I/O or waits for some event

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: When the I/O or event completes, it moves to the ready state.

questions.question: On a single CPU, how many processes can be in the running state at one instant?
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Many processes may be ready or waiting.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT normally stored in a Process Control Block (PCB)?

options.B: The source code of the program

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The PCB also holds I/O status information such as open files.

questions.question: A context switch involves:

options.A: Switching the computer off and on
options.C: Saving the state of the current process in its PCB and loading the saved state of the next process

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Context-switch time is pure overhead – no useful work is done.

questions.question: The long-term (job) scheduler mainly controls:

options.A: Which ready process gets the CPU next
options.D: The degree of multiprogramming – how many processes are in memory

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It runs much less often than the CPU scheduler.

questions.question: The short-term (CPU) scheduler:

options.A: Selects a process from the ready queue and allocates the CPU to it; it runs very frequently

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: It may run every few milliseconds, so it must be fast.

questions.question: Swapping a partially executed process out of memory and later back in is done by the:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Swapping reduces the degree of multiprogramming temporarily.

questions.question: A process that spends more time doing I/O than computation is called:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: The long-term scheduler should admit a good mix of I/O-bound and CPU-bound processes.

questions.question: Memory allocated dynamically at run time (e.g. with malloc or new) comes from the process's:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: The heap grows upward; the stack, holding local variables and return addresses, grows downward.

questions.question: Local variables and function parameters of a process are kept in its:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Global variables are in the data section.

questions.question: The module that gives control of the CPU to the process chosen by the short-term scheduler is the:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The time it takes is called dispatch latency.

questions.question: In the seven-state process model, a process that is swapped out to disk while waiting for an event is in the:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Stallings: Ready/Suspend and Blocked/Suspend are the two suspended states.

questions.question: The queue of all processes residing in main memory and waiting to execute is the:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Processes waiting for a particular I/O device are in that device's queue.

questions.question:
Match the scheduler with its job:
a. Long-term scheduler
b. Short-term scheduler
c. Medium-term scheduler
d. Dispatcher

1. Switches context and jumps to the user program
2. Swaps processes out of and into memory
3. Selects jobs from the pool to load into memory
4. Selects a process from the ready queue
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Scheduler matching appears in KSET papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A program is a passive entity, while a process is an active entity.
II. Two processes can never run the same program.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: Several users can run separate processes of the same program, e.g. a browser.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Context-switch time is pure overhead.
Reason (R): The system does no useful work for any user process while switching.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: That is why context switches should be fast and not too frequent.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When its I/O completes, a waiting process moves directly to the running state.
Reason (R): After its I/O completes, a process is placed in the ready queue.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: It goes to ready and must wait for the scheduler, so A is false.

questions.question: A newly created process that the OS has not yet admitted to the pool of executable processes is in the:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: The long-term scheduler admits it to the ready state.

questions.question: Which transition can occur directly in the five-state process model?
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Waiting processes must first become ready.

questions.question: The time the dispatcher takes to stop one process and start another is called:
questions.subject: Process Concept, States, PCB and Schedulers
questions.explanation: It should be as short as possible.

options.A: Wait indefinitely until there is room in the mailbox
options.C: Do not wait at all but rather return immediately

questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication

questions.question: The OS environment which permits many processors active at the same time is.

questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q73

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of technique in which dumb terminals are connected to a central computer system?
questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: Many users at terminals share one central computer in time slices. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)
questions.source: GTTC 2024 Technician Gr-III CS (C1) · Q78

questions.question:
Match the following:
i. Context switching
ii. Semaphores
iii. Process synchronization
iv. Message passing
(a) process communicate by sending and receiving messages
(b) co-ordination of the execution of multiple processes sharing the resources
(c) enables multiple processes to share a single CPU
(d) helps to prevent race condition

options.A: i – a, ii – b, iii – c, iv – d
options.B: i – b, ii – c, iii – d, iv – a
options.C: i – c, ii – d, iii – b, iv – a

questions.question: In UNIX, the fork() system call:

options.A: Replaces the current program with a new one
options.B: Creates a child process that is a copy of the parent; it returns 0 in the child and the child's PID in the parent

questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A negative return value means fork() failed.

questions.question: If a program calls fork() three times in sequence (each call made by every existing process), the total number of processes, including the original, is:
questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each fork doubles the count: 2³ = 8 (7 new child processes).

int main() { fork(); fork(); printf("hello\n"); }

questions.explanation: Two forks give 2² = 4 processes, and each prints once.

questions.question: The exec() family of system calls:

options.C: Replaces the calling process's memory image with a new program

questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: fork() followed by exec() is how a shell runs a command.

questions.question: A parent process waits for its child to finish by calling:
questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: wait() also collects the child's exit status.

questions.question: A process that has terminated but whose parent has not yet called wait() is a(n):
questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Its entry stays in the process table until the parent collects the exit status.

questions.question: A process whose parent has terminated without waiting for it is a(n):

options.C: Orphan process – adopted by init (systemd) in Linux

questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). init periodically calls wait() to clean up such children.

questions.question: When a parent terminates, some systems also terminate all its children. This is called:
questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: It is normally initiated by the operating system.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason for allowing processes to cooperate?

options.A: To increase the number of system crashes

questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
questions.explanation: Cooperating processes need IPC.

questions.question: The two fundamental models of interprocess communication are:
questions.subject: Process Operations, IPC and Client–Server Communication
